rules.statement: A person who expends money or labour in improving property, intending to do so for his own benefit, thinking either that the property belongs to himself, or that he has the right to occupy it for some substantial period, whereas in fact he has no such right or title to the property and in consequence the improvements are acquired by the owner of the property, is entitled to claim from the latter the amount by which the property has been enhanced in value.
rules.supporting_quote: Wille in Principles of South African Law (1937 edition), page 353 sets out the right to improvements to property as follows : - "A person who expends money or labour in improving property, intending to do so for his own benefit, thinking either that the property belongs to himself, or that he has the right to occupy it for some substantial period, whereas in fact he has no such right or title to the property and in consequence the improvements are . acquired by the owner of the property, is entitled to claim from the latter the amount by which the property has been enhanced in value.
